peace_force_personnel.constitutional_ceiling: 1,000,000 or 0.0125% of world population (~12 per 100,000), whichever is lower
peace_force_personnel.basis: UN peacekeeping uniformed peak 106,595 (Mar 2015) deployed at once; sustaining that deployment needs ~3x total strength for rotation/training/reserve (planning ASSUMPTION, not verified) => ~320k; plus a surge reserve for 2-3 simultaneous Haiti-scale disasters (US alone deployed 21,493 in 2 weeks, 2010) and logistics/airlift/verification of WMD destruction. Central 500k. Low 250k assumes Protection Service carries most disaster work and the disarmed world needs less than the 2015 PK peak. High = ceiling for transition years when residual armed groups persist.

peace_force_budget_pct_world_gdp.unit: % of world GDP (2025 world GDP ~USD 115.5 tn implied by SIPRI)
peace_force_budget_pct_world_gdp.basis: UN PK cost per uniformed peacekeeper USD 94k (2024-25: 5.6bn/59,376) and 79k (2014-15); world milex per armed-forces member USD 105k (2,887bn/27.4m). UN costs understate a fairly paid force (troop reimbursement only USD 1,428/month), hence 100-150k all-in.

freed_personnel.basis: World Bank armed forces 27,406,000 (2020) minus Peace Force size. Freed people are offered work in health, construction, civil protection (Art. 5.3); some move to regional police and the Protection Service.

freed_spending_pct_gdp.basis: SIPRI 2025 military burden 2.5% of world GDP minus Peace Force budget. Gross figure: excludes transition costs (income guarantee for 27m former soldiers, WMD destruction/verification, possible police expansion in under-policed regions).

regional_police_reference.un_recommended_222_status: UNVERIFIED - no UN document found; do not cite
regional_police_reference.note: Regional civilian police are separate from and ~50x larger than the central Peace Force - a structural counterweight (De Bruin 2018).

safeguards: Hard constitutional ceiling on personnel (<=0.0125% of world population) and budget (<=0.15% of world GDP); actual level set by law below it and published annually (Art. 5a.4).
Multinational composition: no region >5% of personnel or commanders (UN PK already draws on 121 countries).
Commanders rotate every 3 years; members never serve in their own region.
Deployment only with Court ruling + double-majority Council of Regions; 72-hour emergency limit (Art. 5a.2).
Counterweight: armed regional civilian police (~24m worldwide) remain under regional control; counterbalancing reduces coup success though not attempts (De Bruin 2018).
Civilian oversight + legitimacy + strong civil society lower structural coup risk (Belkin & Schofer 2003).
Separate control of logistics/airlift/arms depots from combat command, and of arms stocks under independent verification (design proposal, not evidence-tested).
Transition is the risk window: new forces raise coup-attempt odds the next year (De Bruin 2018) - phase build-up gradually with independent inspection.
Annual public register of size, budget, every deployment; independent inspectorate reporting to the Court and Council of Regions.
